text: Build job 6 of the records-history plan (docs/design/records-history.md section 9, decision D111): incremental checking. After a passing local attribution check (athena check --attribution, and athena land after a landing record), write a checkpoint record to athena/records with the records writer, naming the last passing main commit, the records-branch tip it was judged against, and the check's version; a later check judges only main's commits and records added since the newest checkpoint. A full-replay mode ignores checkpoints, judges everything from the start, and fails if it disagrees with the newest checkpoint. CI's token is read-only, so CI never writes checkpoints: its attribution job reads the newest one and runs incrementally on pushes, and as a full replay on its weekly schedule. Each run reports seconds taken and the number of commits and records judged. Tests: an incremental run judges only the new commits; a tampered checkpoint (naming a commit the full replay fails) is caught by the replay; a check-version change forces a full replay; a failing check writes no checkpoint. Timing: a producer's working copy has no history of this repository, so time a full replay and an incremental run on a synthetic repository of about 200 landings in a test or bench and report them as measured on that fixture; the timing on this repository is taken after landing, outside this job. This repeats job 20261024-220048-engm, which stopped because its request asked for timing here.
